headline: CVR Energy to buy Marathon's Midcontinent refineries for $4.2B
intro: Oil's whipsawing on Iran headlines again, but the real refined-fuels story is consolidation — CVR just bought its way to 384,000 b/d of Midcontinent throughput while New Jersey tells Washington it can keep its Russian diesel loophole to itself.
overview: Crude sold off sharply as Iran signaled openness to talks, dragging crack spreads and product prices along for the ride, while EIA data showed global refinery throughput still recovering from a 4.8 million b/d hit tied to the Middle East conflict. On the deals front, CVR Energy's $4.2B acquisition of Marathon's Midcontinent refineries is the biggest refining-sector move, and policy friction is building as New Jersey moves to block Russian diesel cargoes the Trump administration has authorized. Clean-fuels activity continued apace with new SAF and renewable diesel supply deals from Phillips 66, Shell, and a data-center backup-power pilot.

stories.title: CVR Energy to acquire Midcontinent refineries from Marathon Petroleum in $4.2-billion deal
stories.summary: CVR Energy will acquire Marathon Petroleum's Midcontinent refineries in a $4.2 billion deal, boosting CVR's crude throughput capacity to about 384,000 b/d and generating an estimated $70 million in annual run-rate synergies.

stories.title: NJ Governor Bars Entry of Russian Diesel Allowed by Trump
stories.summary: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill warned state port and terminal operators against accepting Russian diesel shipments that the Trump administration has authorized.

stories.title: Global refinery inputs fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 before modest recovery
stories.summary: Global crude refinery inputs fell 4.8 million b/d (6%) in Q2 2026 after Middle East conflict began in late February, per EIA/Kpler data, before rebounding 1.8 million b/d in Q3 as refiners adjusted trade flows.

stories.title: Refinery Trouble And Global Conflict Keep Energy Markets Guessing
stories.summary: Energy markets swung from overnight gains to losses amid refinery trouble and ongoing global conflict headlines, per TACenergy's morning market talk.

stories.title: Oil Prices Sink as Iran Signals Talks
stories.summary: Oil prices plunged more than 7% as Washington and Tehran signaled openness to renewed peace negotiations.

stories.title: Oil Plunges as Iran Opens Door to Talks
stories.summary: Brent crude reacted sharply lower in Monday trading as Iran signaled openness to renewed talks with the U.S.

stories.title: US, Iran Restore Diplomacy amid Limited Strikes
stories.summary: Iran and the U.S. are reviewing fresh mediator proposals aimed at avoiding a return to all-out war, according to a briefed diplomat.

stories.title: Aramco Logs 9 Pct Higher Profit
stories.summary: Aramco posted a 9% rise in Q3 profit, helped by a jump in refining earnings as the Iran conflict pushed oil prices higher.

stories.title: RTI supplies Phillips 66 with ISCC-certified used cooking oil for SAF production
stories.summary: Restaurant Technologies will supply Phillips 66 with ISCC-certified used cooking oil for SAF production, part of broader value-chain efforts to scale lower-carbon fuels.

stories.title: Shell signs long-term SAF offtake agreement with Green Sky Manara
stories.summary: Shell signed a long-term SAF offtake agreement with Green Sky Manara's Port Nador, Morocco facility, expected to start up in October 2028 with 150,000 tpy capacity.

stories.title: Sabey Data Centers pilots renewable diesel for backup power at Austin, Texas, site
stories.summary: Sabey Data Centers is piloting renewable diesel for backup power at its Austin, Texas site, targeting a hard-to-reduce source of scope 1 emissions.

stories.title: Canada’s wood waste could supply 5 times its jet-fuel demand, new white paper finds
stories.summary: A Sustaero white paper presented at AFCC finds Canada's wood waste could supply five times the country's jet-fuel demand, with hydrogen-enhanced conversion key to unlocking low-cost forest residues.

stories.title: Tidewater to combine midstream, renewables into 1 company
stories.summary: Tidewater is combining its midstream and renewables businesses into one company, operating as Tidewater Midstream and Infrastructure Ltd. on the TSX under symbol TWM.

stories.title: Envision marks its 1st international application of SAFc at Western Australia event
stories.summary: Envision marked its first international application of SAFc at a Western Australia event, providing environmental attributes for 10 tons of CO2-emissions reductions.

## MPC 10-Q (Q3 2026) — Refined Fuels Market Takeaways

- **Refining margins surged on supply disruption**: R&M segment adjusted EBITDA exploded to $9,895M in Q3'26 vs. $1,762M in Q3'25 (9mo: $17,927M vs. $4,141M), driven by "higher realized refining margins supported by stable demand and higher product prices driven by global crude oil supply disruptions" (Middle East, Russia). Refined product revenue rose to $50,298M from $30,525M YoY. decks.analysis:
## Marathon Petroleum Q3 2026 — Refined Fuels Market Takeaways

- **Record capture economics**: R&M margin hit $45.70/bbl (vs. $17.60/bbl Q3'25) and segment adjusted EBITDA reached $34.15/bbl (vs. $6.37/bbl), with refining operating costs essentially flat at $5.60/bbl — indicating the gain was almost entirely crack-spread/market-driven rather than cost efficiency, and was broad-based across regions (Gulf Coast $43.46/bbl, Mid-Con $47.33/bbl, West Coast $47.46/bbl margins, all roughly tripling YoY).
- **Utilization at max**: Crude capacity utilization was 100% (vs. 95% Q3'25), with total throughput of 3.2 MMbpd — system running flat-out to capture the margin environment; Q4'26 guidance implies a step-down to 3,080 mbpd total throughput (2,830 mbpd crude).
- **Renewable diesel swung decisively positive**: Segment adjusted EBITDA $254M vs. $(56)M a year ago, driven by stronger margins, improved regulatory credit values (LCFS/RIN-type), and higher throughput; RD margin rose to $304M from just $8M.

decks.title: 8-K exhibit d399885dex992.htm (filed 2026-11-03)
decks.analysis:
# Refined Fuels Market Analysis: Mandan/SPP Carve-Out (MPC → CVR Energy)

- **Capacity & footprint**: Combined 177,000 bpcd crude refining capacity — SPP (MN) at 105,000 bpcd processing sweet/heavy sour crude, and Mandan (ND) at 72,000 bpcd running North Dakota sweet crude. No throughput/utilization rates disclosed, only nameplate capacity.

- **Margin strength**: 9-month 2026 net income nearly tripled to $697M (vs. $267M in 2025) on revenue growth of only ~30% ($7,605M vs. $5,850M), implying significant crack-spread/capture improvement rather than volume-driven gains. Gasoline revenue rose to $3,826M (from $2,921M) and distillates to $2,939M (from $2,016M), the two largest product lines.

- **RIN/RFS exposure is material but partially hedged by SRE credits**: Environmental obligations more than doubled to $108M (from $46M), driven by $230M of incremental RFS compliance accruals for the 2026 period, offset by a $46M settlement of the 2025 RFS obligation and Mandan small-refinery-exemption (SRE) credits that reduced obligations by $122M (2026) and $114M (2025) — underscoring continued reliance on SRE relief to manage RIN cost burden.

- **No renewable diesel/SAF disclosure**: The filing shows no renewable diesel or SA
